observation: Native crop shows the historical st ligature in the word rendered by Transkribus as ὕϛερον; DocAI emits ὕςερον and Vision ὕτερον. This is useful complementary glyph output. Adjacent letters and the cropped neighbour differ, so this is not a reference transcription.

The crop visibly contains several printed rows. The imposed single-line Transkribus reading loses the readable row structure and returns mostly capital fragments, whereas both Google readings preserve several rows. This limits the supplied-line geometry on known multi-line failures.
The native kai sign lies between ὁπλιτῶν and τῶν. DocAI writes κὶ, Vision writes καὶ, and Transkribus emits a comma at that position. None preserves ϗ in this example.
The native kai sign after τέρων is returned as κὶ by DocAI, καὶ by Vision, and ἢ by Transkribus. These readings do not preserve the sign as ϗ.
